title: Tamsin and the Drop
premise: Paloma Thornbury, a burned-out private security contractor hiding from her past, receives a calendar invite to a meeting sent by a handler who died six months ago. The meeting leads her to Ilse Brandt, a defector carrying evidence that a Frankfurt bank laundered money for the syndicate Paloma once served—and that her old team was murdered to bury it. As Paloma extracts Ilse across Europe before markets open, she realizes Ilse may be deliberate bait designed to flush out anyone still loyal to the truth. In the end, Paloma chooses exposure over escape, broadcasting the evidence at the cost of her anonymity, and finds an unexpected found family in Ilse and a disgraced journalist who help her survive what comes after.
about_author: Beatrix Dunmore is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients she never met. She lives off-grid on the Cornish coast, where she writes thrillers about people who know too much.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Insomniac and invisible, Paloma works small contracts in Lisbon until a calendar notification appears: a meeting tomorrow, organized by Marcus Webb—her dead handler. She verifies it isn't spam, then can't stop checking. Emotional beat: dread curdling into compulsion; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Slot
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She stakes out the meeting location—a shuttered shipping office—expecting a trap. Instead she finds a courier who hands over a burner phone and a photo of Ilse Brandt, plus one sentence: 'Frankfurt opens at nine.' Emotional beat: wary curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Introduce Ilse hiding in a Rotterdam safehouse, memorizing ledger fragments linking the Hessler Bank to the Vory-linked Koltsov network. She doesn't trust her new contact, only the dead man who arranged it. Emotional beat: exhausted resolve; she is ready to be spent like currency.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma meets Ilse, tests her story against what she knows of Webb's operations, and finds it holds—too well. She takes the job for reasons she won't name. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment; loyalty reawakening like a healed wound itching.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Route planning through Antwerp while Paloma notices surveillance that's too competent to be police. A tail she kills reveals a Koltsov signal device. Someone knew the meet location. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into professional focus.

chapters.title: What Webb Knew
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, flashback interwoven. Decoding Webb's dead-drop cache, Paloma reconstructs his final weeks: he'd discovered the 'incident' that broke her sleep wasn't an accident but a sanctioned cleanup. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Bait Theory
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse confesses her suspicion: Koltsov let her defect because her evidence is incomplete without a second key—held by someone inside Paloma's old firm. She may be the lure. Emotional beat: guilt and honesty forging fragile trust between the two women.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma contacts Declan Okafor, a disgraced financial reporter who once burned a source to save himself. He confirms Hessler's structure and offers his remaining contacts—if she lets him publish. Emotional beat: transactional alliance, both testing whether the other is salvageable.

chapters.title: Antwerp Nightfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. First extraction leg goes wrong when a safehouse burns hours after they leave. Paloma realizes the leak is close—someone reading her tradecraft like a signature. Emotional beat: hunted intimacy; trust becomes tactical necessity.

chapters.title: Old Team, New Orders
chapters.summary: Villain POV (Keller, Paloma's former colleague now running Koltsov's wet work). Keller tracks the pair, genuinely regretful—he liked Paloma—but the firm's survival requires her death. Emotional beat: chilling banality; betrayal as routine business.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals the full design: Webb hid the second key inside Paloma's own incident file, betting she'd be the only one motivated enough to dig it out. Paloma was always part of the plan. Emotional beat: fury transmuting into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With twelve hours to market open, they race toward Frankfurt where a Hessler insider will authenticate the ledger if the key matches. Keller's team converges. Emotional beat: countdown pressure compressing every relationship to its essence.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. Declan discovers his editor has been feeding Koltsov information for years; his redemption arc collides with his oldest sin. He must decide whom to warn first. Emotional beat: shame confronted; choosing the harder right.

chapters.title: Main Station
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Frankfurt Hauptbahnhof handoff collapses into a staged arrest—Keller using German police as unwitting cover. Paloma sacrifices their route to keep Ilse free, getting taken herself. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of changed loyalties.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV (captive). Keller offers Paloma her old life back if she surrenders the key. Their conversation becomes a trial of everything the firm taught her. Emotional beat: the book's thematic core—loyalty vs. truth laid bare across a table.

chapters.title: Ilse Alone
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse could flee with partial evidence and live. Instead she contacts Declan and plans an extraction worthy of the woman who saved her. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing; courage borrowed and repaid.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Ilse trades herself for Paloma via a brokered swap—then springs the real plan: Declan has already moved the authentication window. Keller realizes too late he's been managing a decoy. Emotional beat: reversal joy; the hunted becoming architects.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the Hessler authentication, the insider balks; Paloma forces the match publicly as markets open and the ledger hits Declan's wire simultaneously. Koltsov's positions begin bleeding. Emotional beat: climax—truth detonating on schedule.

chapters.title: Cleanup Crew
chapters.summary: Keller's POV. Ordered to erase everyone, Keller instead burns his orders and walks, leaving the firm exposed. His last act is deleting Paloma's file from every index. Emotional beat: a villain's quiet defection; even loyalty has limits.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. The story breaks; Hessler executives fall, Koltsov assets freeze, and Declan's byline is restored at the price of never being trusted fully again. Emotional beat: bittersweet vindication; justice outside the law still costs.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. No longer anonymous, Paloma faces hearings and threats but sleeps—truly sleeps—for the first time since the incident. She declines protection detail, choosing her own. Emotional beat: release; invisibility traded for integrity.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Drop
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating POVs. Months later, Paloma, Ilse, and Declan share a cautious dinner in Cornwall under Beatrix Dunmore's watchful neighborly eye—the three forming an unlikely unit. A new encrypted message arrives. Paloma smiles. Emotional beat: found family sealed, sequel door ajar.
